title: Arrival Rule for the Appraisal Order Complexity Add-On
content:
Appraisal Order complexity add-on — arrival rule for the completed report.

The arrival rule of the complexity add-on compares the completed date with the due date in calendar days: a report completed 3 days or more after its due date carries only the living-area part; a report completed 1 or 2 days after its due date carries the add-on subtotal less 100 dollars, but never less than the living-area part; and a report completed on or before its due date carries the whole add-on subtotal. The arrival rule is applied to the add-on subtotal — all the parts of the complexity add-on added together — and what it yields is the complexity add-on.

The complexity add-on is built from its parts, in place of the report type's gross-living-area surcharge alone, and is reduced by two things only, its arrival rule and any amount already standing on its own line; the update visit charge and the final inspection charge stack their own parts under their own rules, and every other appraisal charge is still charged at its own amount with no stacking or discount.

**Input — judgement — output.**

| Completed date against due date (calendar days) | Complexity add-on |
|---|---|
| On or before the due date | The whole add-on subtotal |
| 1 or 2 days after | The add-on subtotal less 100.00, or the living-area part if that is higher |
| 3 days or more after | The living-area part alone; the other parts are dropped |

**Worked figures (hypothetical: add-on subtotal 330.00, of which the living-area part is 210.00).**
- Completed on the due date: 330.00.
- Completed 2 days after the due date: 330.00 less 100.00, that is 230.00, which is not below 210.00, so 230.00.
- Completed 3 days after the due date: 210.00.

*Second hypothetical:* add-on subtotal 250.00, living-area part 210.00, completed 1 day after the due date: 250.00 less 100.00 is 150.00, below 210.00, so the add-on is 210.00.

Both dates are those on the Appraisal Order: the due date (the date the completed report is promised) and the completed date (the date the completed report was received).
